welcome.description: A summary of your overall financial state: how much liquid money you have, how much you owe on credit cards, how close you are to your budget, and which payments are coming up.
bullets: See your liquidity and revolving debt at a glance
Compare your spending against the month's and week's budget
Check which payments are due soon before they catch you off guard

steps.title: Your available money
steps.text: Adds up the balance of your cash/bank-type accounts -- it doesn't include credit cards, those are debt, not liquidity.

steps.title: Payments in the next 3 days
steps.text: Combines recurring expenses and debt payments due very soon -- only shows up when something's that close.

steps.title: How close you are to the limit
steps.text: The color goes from green to orange to red based on what percentage of the month's budget you've already spent.

steps.title: Income and expenses for the month
steps.text: Only shows up once you generate the month's report in Reports -- compared against the previous month.

steps.title: This week's cash flow
steps.text: Income vs. expenses over the last 7 days, to quickly notice if you're spending more than you're bringing in this week.

steps.title: Net worth
steps.text: Joins together the monthly reports you've already generated -- you need at least 2 months of reports to see the trend line.

steps.title: Highlighted insights
steps.text: The most relevant observations generated by the automatic analysis -- click to see them all in Insights.

steps.title: Upcoming payments
steps.text: Combines your active recurring expenses with debt payments due in the coming days, so nothing takes you by surprise.

welcome.description: Your real accounts: banks, cash, and credit cards. Net worth is calculated by adding up the balance of all of them.
bullets: Register bank, savings, cash, or credit card accounts
Customize each one with a logo and color
Check the transaction history of any account

steps.title: Add an account
steps.text: Bank, savings, cash, or credit card -- the latter is registered as a liability (what you owe), not as available money. It's not the same as a Debt: that's for loans, not for cards.

steps.title: Assets and liabilities
steps.text: Your accounts are grouped into Assets (your money) and Liabilities (credit cards). The net worth below is the difference between the two.

steps.title: Account transactions
steps.text: Select any account on the left to see its full history here, with a search box and an in/out filter. Editing the starting balance of an account with transactions recalculates the current balance and confirms it with you first.

steps.title: Your card's cycle
steps.text: Closing date, payment due limit, current cycle balance, and available credit -- these come from the data you gave the card when you created it. If you have active interest-free installments (Meses Sin Intereses), you'll see right here how many there are and how much they commit this month, and each one carries an "MSI paid/total" tag on its row in the history.

steps.title: Edit, pay, reconcile, or delete
steps.text: Editing changes the account's data. On a credit card, "Pay card" registers a real transfer from any other account -- that's the only place you pay it, it no longer exists as a separate Debt. Reconcile balance (liquid accounts only) adjusts the difference between what you registered and the real amount by creating a visible transaction -- use it when the balance doesn't add up, not to correct the starting balance. Delete is permanent.

welcome.description: The full history of your transactions: income, expenses, transfers, and loans. You can filter by account, type, date, or text.
bullets: Register income, expenses, and transfers between accounts
Split a shared expense and collect your part later
Filter by account, text, or a specific day on the calendar

steps.title: Register a transaction
steps.text: For income or an expense you just pick the account, category, and amount -- the app resolves the accounting counterpart on its own. If the expense is on a credit card, the option "Interest-free installments?" (Meses Sin Intereses) appears so you can mark it as MSI and track its progress later in Accounts.

steps.title: Pay a card
steps.text: Register the payment from any other account of yours, without leaving Transactions -- it only appears if you have at least one credit card registered. If you have several, you pick which one first.

steps.title: Shared expense
steps.text: Register the total charge, your real share, and each person's share -- what's owed to you shows up as "they owe me" in Debts. Once created, it can no longer be edited (only deleted), since it involves more than two internal transactions.

steps.title: Find what you're looking for
steps.text: Search by text or filter by account -- the list below updates instantly.

steps.title: Sort by date
steps.text: Click the header to switch the order between most recent and oldest first.

steps.title: Edit or delete
steps.text: Some transactions (like shared expenses) can no longer be edited, only deleted -- if the pencil is missing, that's why.

steps.title: Calendar view
steps.text: The same data as a calendar -- click a day to automatically filter the list to that day, and click again to remove the filter.

welcome.description: How much you plan to spend per variable expense category (food, transport, etc.) each month, against what you've actually spent.
bullets: Set a monthly cap on any category, one at a time, it's optional
Get a suggested limit based on your average spending
Browse past months to see how you did

steps.title: Set a limit
steps.text: If you don't set a limit on any category, nothing shows up in the breakdown -- it's optional, category by category.

steps.title: Automatic suggestion
steps.text: When your average spending over the last 3 months drifts away from your current limit, this shortcut appears to match it with one click.

steps.title: What you have left
steps.text: Estimated income minus fixed commitments (debts and recurring expenses) minus what's spent. Red if you've already gone over.

steps.title: Fixed commitments
steps.text: The sum of your active debts and recurring expenses -- money you already know you're going to spend this month, regardless of the variable budget.

steps.title: Categories near the limit
steps.text: Only shows up if something's about to go over -- a quick heads-up without checking category by category.

steps.title: Spending distribution
steps.text: How this month's spending is split across your categories with a limit.

steps.title: Trend over up to 12 months
steps.text: % of your budget used month by month -- useful for seeing if you're improving or getting worse over time.

steps.title: Review past months
steps.text: The weekly view and the limit alert only apply to the current month -- a closed month no longer has a "current week."

welcome.description: Everything that involves owing money, in either direction: personal loans, formal or informal, or something as informal as lending a friend $100. Credit cards live in Accounts -- that's where they're paid and where you see the progress of your installment purchases.
bullets: Register debts with their full plan: amount, frequency, and account
Switch between "I owe" and "They owe me" -- same screen, different direction
Register real payments/collections that move money from an account

steps.title: Register a debt
steps.text: Type (personal loan, payroll loan, informal, civic, or received), amount, installment/frequency, and, if applicable, which account the cash moved from/to when it originated -- optional, for a debt you already had before using the app.

steps.title: Debt with no plan
steps.text: For an overdue or loosely structured debt: just a name and amount. Only appears if you turned on "I have a debt with payment problems" in Settings.

steps.title: Activate it once you have a plan
steps.text: Turns a debt with no plan into one with a full structure (amount, frequency, account) -- you can apply a write-down if you negotiated the amount.

steps.title: Two directions, same screen
steps.text: "I owe" and "They owe me" use the same model -- only who owes whom changes.

steps.title: Correct balance vs. register payment
steps.text: Correct balance adjusts the number without moving real money -- useful when loading old history. Register payment/collection does move money from an account.

steps.title: Your debt overview
steps.text: The total outstanding and, if applicable, how much of that is committed each month. A card with a red border flags an APR above 25%.

welcome.description: Expenses and income that repeat on a fixed cycle -- services, utilities, and recurring income like payroll. Subscriptions (streaming, software) have their own page and don't show up here.
bullets: Register a recurring item and set its billing frequency
Confirm or reject each transaction before it counts as real
Check what's billed in the next 7 days

steps.title: Add a recurring item
steps.text: Services, utilities, or a fixed income like payroll -- set the amount and frequency once. A service marked as essential alerts you daily from the first day it goes unconfirmed, regardless of the urgency you chose.

steps.title: Confirm before it counts
steps.text: As the date approaches, the system prepares the transaction as a draft -- you confirm or reject it before it becomes a real transaction.

steps.title: Edit, pause, or cancel
steps.text: Editing keeps the history. Pausing stops automatic generation without losing the setup. Canceling retires it -- neither one deletes what's already registered.

steps.title: They don't disappear, they get filtered
steps.text: A paused or canceled item isn't deleted from your history -- it just leaves "Active." Change the filter to see it again.

steps.title: What your cards already owe
steps.text: Only shows up if you have credit cards. Adds up the installments of your active installment purchases plus what's spent in the open statement cycle -- it's informational, it doesn't get added to the "Committed / month" above (that spending was already counted in the budget for the month you made it).

steps.title: Breakdown by category
steps.text: How your monthly commitment is split across categories -- only counts active services/utilities, not income.

steps.title: Next 7 days
steps.text: To plan your pay period knowing what's coming.

welcome.description: Your subscriptions (streaming, software, memberships) kept separate from other recurring items, so you can see at a glance how much they cost you per month.
bullets: Register a subscription with its billing frequency
The total converts every frequency to its monthly equivalent
A passive notice reminds you about the ones active for more than 12 months

steps.title: Add a subscription
steps.text: Streaming, software, or any membership -- amount, frequency, and the account it's charged from.

steps.title: How much it costs you per month
steps.text: Since not all of them bill monthly (some are yearly), the total converts each frequency to its monthly equivalent -- each row also shows its own equivalent.

steps.title: Edit, pause, or cancel
steps.text: Editing keeps the history -- useful for when the price goes up, common in streaming and software. Pause and Cancel can be reversed as long as you don't resubscribe elsewhere.

steps.title: Still using it?
steps.text: Starting at 12 months active, a notice asks whether you're really still using it -- purely informational, it doesn't change anything on its own.

steps.title: They don't disappear, they get filtered
steps.text: A paused or canceled subscription stays in your history -- change the filter to see it.

steps.title: Upcoming renewals
steps.text: What renews in the next 7 days, so no charge catches you off guard.

welcome.description: A chat with AI that sees your real financial situation (accounts, debts, budget, transactions) and answers using that as context -- these aren't generic answers.
bullets: Ask anything about your financial situation
It can create transactions, accounts, debts, or recurring items for you -- it always asks you to confirm before saving anything
It doesn't edit or delete anything that already exists, only creates
Attach PDF bank statements to bring in historical data
Ask it to save a plan and you'll see it later in Insights

steps.title: It can also create data for you
steps.text: It doesn't just answer questions -- ask it to log an expense, an account, or a debt and it'll propose the action with a Confirm/Cancel card before saving it.

steps.title: Bring in your bank statements
steps.text: Attach PDFs (even password-protected ones) -- it separates regular charges from installment purchases and avoids duplicates between statements from the same batch.

steps.title: More ways to bring in data
steps.text: Import from Excel, or copy a prompt to hand your data over from another AI (ChatGPT, Gemini) if you already have it there.

steps.title: Ask whatever you want
steps.text: The common-question buttons are just a starting point -- type your real question here.

steps.title: What the AI sees about you
steps.text: Exactly the context it uses to answer: net worth, financial health, this month's commitments, what's available this week, and your latest transactions.

steps.title: Queries left today
steps.text: There's a daily limit to control the cost of the AI -- it resets every day.

welcome.description: Automatic observations about your finances based on your real data: a detected pattern, an alert, a suggestion.
bullets: Generate a new analysis of your current situation
They're also created automatically when you ask the AI Advisor to save a plan
Mark them as resolved or dismiss them once they no longer apply
Every active insight gets reviewed again on its own over time

steps.title: Generate a new analysis
steps.text: Runs the analysis on your current situation and creates insights if it finds something worth pointing out to you.

steps.title: Priority and category
steps.text: The priority (high/medium/low) is just a guide -- it doesn't trigger any extra alert on its own. If it's already been reviewed at least once, "View reviews" compares how your situation has changed since then.

steps.title: Resolved vs. Dismiss
steps.text: "Resolved" is for when you've already handled what it said. "Dismiss" is for when you're not interested. Both remove it from this list and send it to the history below.

steps.title: 10 active max
steps.text: When you resolve or dismiss one, it leaves this list and moves to the history below.

steps.title: Everything you've already seen
steps.text: Resolved or dismissed insights stay here, with their category and date.

welcome.description: Reports for periods that are already closed (last month or last year) -- a frozen "snapshot" of a period that's already over, with analysis generated on those numbers.
bullets: Generate last month's or last year's report whenever you want to see it
Filter between income, expenses, or all transactions
Track your historical net worth across months

steps.title: Generate a report
steps.text: Reports aren't created on their own -- you generate them whenever you want to see them.

steps.title: Monthly or yearly
steps.text: A yearly report needs that year's monthly reports to already exist.

steps.title: Savings rate, DTI, and health
steps.text: The colors follow fixed thresholds: savings rate and DTI (debt vs. income) go from green to red based on how far you are from healthy. Financial health also flags whether it improved or worsened vs. the previous period.

steps.title: Balance adjustments for the period
steps.text: Counts how many times you reconciled a balance in this period -- only shows up if there was at least one.

steps.title: Income, expenses, or all
steps.text: This filter moves both the highlighted category and the "Points for this period" below at the same time.

steps.title: Categories for the period
steps.text: Click a category with subcategories to expand them -- it's not obvious at a glance, but it's clickable.

steps.title: Historical net worth
steps.text: Joins all your generated monthly reports into a single trend line -- it's collapsed by default, click to open it.

steps.title: Regenerate if something changed
steps.text: Recalculates the report you're viewing from scratch with your current transactions -- useful if you generated it before loading old history.

welcome.description: Your profile and your account preferences -- not the settings for one particular screen, but for the whole app.
bullets: Update your profile photo and password
The theme is saved to your account, not to this browser
Delete specific data without losing your account

steps.title: Your profile and password
steps.text: Name, photo, and password -- the same block includes the form to change it. If you signed in with Google, your photo is imported the first time.

steps.title: Theme, notifications, and payment cycle
steps.text: The theme is saved to your account -- if you sign in from another device, it looks the same. Email and push are independent channels, you can turn off just one. The payment cycle feeds Dashboard and Budget.

steps.title: Debt trouble
steps.text: Turn it on if you have an overdue debt you're not paying -- it enables a separate section in Debts and gives that context to the AI Advisor.

steps.title: Google account
steps.text: You can unlink Google, but only if your account also has a password -- otherwise you'd be left with no way to sign in.

steps.title: Start fresh without losing your account
steps.text: Delete everything except accounts, absolutely everything, or just specific categories like transactions or the AI Advisor's history.

steps.title: Delete account
steps.text: Different from "Delete data": this closes your sessions and disables access entirely. It can't be undone.

welcome.description: Every alert the app has generated for you: reports ready, new insights, budget or debt alerts, and reminders for pending payments.
bullets: A colored dot marks what you haven't read
Mark everything as read at once
Each one's icon and color show its type without having to open it
Email and push channels are turned on or off from Settings, not here

steps.title: Mark everything at once
steps.text: Instead of opening them one by one, this marks them all as read instantly.

steps.title: Your list of alerts
steps.text: Click any of them to mark it as read -- the full text is already in the row, there's no separate detail view. The icon and color on the left tell you the type without needing to read it.

steps.title: Running total
steps.text: Counts all your historical notifications -- the list above only shows the 50 most recent.

welcome.description: Here's where you organize where your money goes (and where it comes from). Every transaction belongs to a category, and expense categories can have their own subcategories.
bullets: Create categories with their own color and icon
Group similar expenses into subcategories (a single level)
Compare how much you spend per category each month

steps.title: Income or expenses
steps.text: Switches the entire catalog you see -- only top-level expense categories can have subcategories.

steps.title: Create new categories
steps.text: Give a name, color, and icon to any category you don't have yet -- there are over 150 icons to choose from, grouped by theme.

steps.title: What each category looks like
steps.text: The amount at the top is what's been spent (or received) this month. If it has subcategories, you can expand them to see the detail -- the budget is always set on the parent category, never on the subcategory.

steps.title: System vs. your own
steps.text: System categories can't be deleted, only deactivated for you (they stop showing up for you, without affecting anyone else). The ones you created can be edited or deleted entirely.

steps.title: Breakdown by subcategory
steps.text: Each color in the bar is a different subcategory, compared against the category's direct spending. Hover to see the exact amount.

steps.title: Deactivated categories
steps.text: The ones you deactivated for yourself stay here below, they don't disappear entirely -- reactivate them whenever you want.

steps.title: Questions later?
steps.text: Come back to this icon whenever you want to review all of this again, without having to search for it.
